sections.h2: Where do I file a deed for Greene County land?
sections.html:
File it at the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill, NC 28580. The counter is staffed from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the phone is 252-747-3620. Letters go to PO Box 86.

The register of deeds describes the office as custodian of the county's real estate papers and vital records. On the land side it handles deeds, deeds of trust, maps, easements, leases, assignments and UCC fixture filings tied to real property. Notary commissions are logged there, and the office swears in notaries who reside in the county.

The county's rate page names three towns, Hookerton, Snow Hill and Walstonburg, and land in any of them is recorded at this single office.

sections.h2: Why does Greene County want a tax form before it records a deed?
sections.html:
The county ties recording to its tax records. Every deed submitted must carry a form signed off by the Greene County Tax Office, which the register of deeds' page calls the Deed Information form.

  • Who is giving and who is receiving the property, with addresses.
  • The street address and legal description, and buildings if the deed splits a parcel.
  • Any personal property that moves with the land, such as a mobile home.
  • Whether deferred tax value is involved, and how the two parties are related if so.
  • Unpaid prior-year tax and the current-year figure, filled in by the tax office.

The tax office also marks the document as a transfer, a split or a merge and assigns the parcel number. Instructions on the reverse of the form cover deeds where delinquent taxes exist, so phone the tax office at 252-747-3615 before heading to the courthouse if you owe back tax on the parcel.

sections.h2: Can a Greene County deed be e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes, for nearly every deed. The office accepts electronic recording for all instruments except maps and highway rights-of-way, so a closing attorney can file from a distance.

The one difference involves the tax form. For electronic filings, the county says its tax office only approves Deed Information sheets inside the e-recording platform and asks filers not to deliver anything to the tax office by hand or mail. Paper filers get the signature first, then bring the packet to Snow Hill.

Index searches run from 1875 to the present on a site run by Courthouse Computer Systems. The register of deeds moved to that system in December 2025, and staff take questions at 252-747-3620.

sections.h2: What will the state fee schedule cost on a Greene County filing?
sections.html:
The charges come from G.S. 161-10 and are uniform statewide. A general instrument is $26.00 for its first 15 pages, a deed of trust is $64.00 for its first 35, and each extra page after those thresholds adds $4.00.

Recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust costs nothing, and plats run $21.00 a sheet. Items outside land records are priced separately by the county: a certified birth, death or marriage copy is $10.00 in cash, and a marriage license is $60, cash only.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise tax when a Greene County house is sold?
sections.html:
The seller does. The state levies $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or value, with a partial $500 counted whole (G.S. 105-228.30), and the transferor settles it with the register of deeds before the deed is filed.

The money is split between the county general fund and the state. Since the tax tracks the amount stated in the deed, check that figure against the sale contract. A deed bounced for a missing tax form or a wrong amount is not effective against later buyers and lien creditors until it is properly registered, according to G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: What do Greene County tax rates and fees look like?
sections.html:
The tax department's 2026 page lists a county rate of $0.7835 per $100, with town and fire district charges stacked on top. The tax office is at 229 Kingold Boulevard, Suite B, Snow Hill (PO Box 482), phone 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

Eleven fire districts are listed, from Arba at $0.0700 to Fort Run at $0.1220, and a Middle Swamp service district shows $0.0910. Owners who hold mobile homes, boats, aircraft or unlicensed vehicles on January 1 must list them during January, and a late listing draws a ten percent penalty.

sections.h2: What else does the Greene County Register of Deeds handle besides deeds?
sections.html:
Vital records and licenses take up much of the counter. A certified birth, death or marriage copy costs $10.00 in cash when requested in person with a photo ID issued by the DMV.

  • By mail: send the signed application, a copy of your state photo ID, a $10.00 money order payable to the Greene County Register of Deeds (personal checks are refused) and a stamped return envelope to PO Box 86, Snow Hill, NC 28580.
  • Marriage license: each applicant 18 or older needs a certified birth certificate, a state photo ID or a passport for non-residents, a Social Security card, and a divorce decree or a spouse's death certificate if previously married. The fee is $60, cash only, and licenses are issued between 9:00 AM and 4:00 PM.
  • Licenses go back to the county that issued them, wherever the wedding takes place.

The office also offers a Thank-A-Vet program, an assumed business name filing, and a link for protection from property and mortgage fraud on its main page.

sections.h2: What does deferred tax mean on the Greene County deed form?
sections.html:
Item six on the county form asks whether deferred value is involved and, if so, how the grantor is related to the grantee. Item seven lists deferred taxes due by year, and the form warns that deferred taxes have not been calculated unless that section is filled in.

The tax office completes the lines for prior-year and current-year tax. If your parcel carries deferred value, ask the office to calculate the amount before the deed is signed, since the form treats uncalculated deferred taxes as unknown. Sellers should not leave that question for the closing table.

The form also asks for Social Security numbers but says disclosure is voluntary, based on federal law and N.C.G.S. 105-309 for tax administration.

sections.h2: How large and how affordable is Greene County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 20,700 residents in 2025, a 1.2% gain on the 2020 estimates base, spread across about 267 square miles of land. That averages roughly 77 residents per square mile.

  • Owner-occupied share of homes: 66.5% (2020 to 2024).
  • Middle value of an owner's home: $117,400.
  • Middle gross rent: $853.
  • Middle household income: $53,244.
  • People in poverty: 19.9%.
  • Housing units in 2025: 8,070.

The middle home value here is about half that listed for Granville County and Greensboro on the same QuickFacts table. Building permits numbered 59 in 2025. Treat these as county averages, since one farmhouse or town lot can sit far from them.

faqs.q: Which office records Greene County deeds?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds in the Greene County Courthouse, 301 N. Greene Street, Snow Hill. It opens 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays except holidays and takes e-recordings for everything but maps and highway rights-of-way.

faqs.q: Does the Greene County tax office sign off on deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's page states that every deed needs a tax form signed by the Tax Office. E-filers get that approval through the electronic platform.

faqs.q: How is the deed excise tax figured here?
faqs.a: At $1.00 per $500 of the consideration or value, with any remainder counted as a full $500. The seller pays the register of deeds before recording.

faqs.q: What number do I call for the register of deeds?
faqs.a: 252-747-3620. The tax office has its own line, 252-747-3615, open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays.

faqs.q: How old are the online Greene County indexes?
faqs.a: The county says online index searches cover 1875 through the present. The office began using a new records system in December 2025.
